relationships.subject: Vincristine
relationships.evidence_quote: Together, these results indicate that vincristine does not prime the NLPR3 inflammasome, but instead functions as a bona fide activation signal for NLRP3 signaling.

relationships.subject: NLRP3
relationships.evidence_quote: Nlrp3 deficiency indeed prevented vincristine-induced mechanical allodynia (Fig. 3 A and Table S2) and gait abnormalities (Fig. 3 B and Table S3).

relationships.subject: MCC950
relationships.evidence_quote: C57BL6/J mice treated with the selective NLRP3 inhibitor MCC950 (Coll et al., 2019) were protected from both mechanical allodynia (Fig. 3 A and Table S2) and gait abnormalities (Fig. 3 B and Table S3) induced by vincristine.

relationships.subject: Vincristine
relationships.evidence_quote: In WT BMMs, vincristine induced IL-1β release (106.8 ± 22.2 pg/ml; Fig. 3 G) and cleavage of pro–IL-1β, caspase-1, and GSDMD (Fig. 3 H).

relationships.subject: Macrophages
relationships.evidence_quote: Macrophages, and not neutrophils, are thus key cellular drivers of VIPN.

relationships.subject: Gasdermin D
relationships.evidence_quote: Indeed, vincristine-induced mechanical allodynia was significantly reduced (P < 0.05, repeated measures two-way ANOVA with Sidak’s multiple comparison correction) in Ice−/− and Gsdmd−/− animals, but not in Casp11−/−, compared with wt controls

relationships.subject: Anakinra
relationships.evidence_quote: Anakinra significantly decreased mechanical hypersensitivity (Fig. 7 A and Table S10), with significantly higher PWT values in the anakinra-treated group relative to the vehicle-treated group at all time points.

key_findings: Vincristine neuropathy is driven by macrophage canonical NLRP3/caspase-1/GSDMD activation and IL-1beta release
